headline: Benchmarking structural variant imputation, haplotype assembly, and repeat genotyping
label: Genomic Analysis Tools And Benchmarks
summary: Recent long-read assemblies and pangenome graphs supply reference data for quantifying how well tools recover structural and repetitive variation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation of methods and resources for structural and repetitive variation. A benchmark of five imputation programs across 52 experimentally genotyped human inversions finds 40-76% imputable, with Minimac4 and IMPUTE5 performing best. RFhap phases long reads by parental k-mer markers and a random forest before assembly, nearly doubling haplotype NG50 and halving switch error. TandemTwister provides parallelized copy-number genotyping of tandem repeats, reporting 99.4% recall on PacBio HiFi data. TEvarSim generates TE-containing genomes with VCF ground truth for benchmarking TE variant detection. A Holstein phased pangenome graph built from 40 haploid assemblies improves structural variant genotyping and GWAS-based trait mapping in dairy cattle. What is new is reference-based quantification of how well inversion imputation and haplotype-resolved assembly recover structural variation.
